messages.author: a68f4a219f644d0b
messages.subject: inla.posterior.sample.eval specific element of Predictor
parts:
Hi,

I am running R 4.2.2 with INLA 23.02.04 (I've also tried the latest stable version, same applies).

I have encountered an issue with using the selection argument with inla.posterior.sample,

samples=inla.posterior.sample(n=nsamp, result=m1, selection = list(Predictor=33))

This could come handy for sampling from specific predictors.
The line itself works, but when I try to access the samples using 

inla.posterior.sample.eval(function(...) {Predictor}, samples),

I get this error: 
"Warning message:
In parallel::mclapply(..., mc.cores = mc.cores) :
  all scheduled cores encountered errors in user code"

In version 21 of R-INLA, the above code worked fine.

In INLA 23.02.04, if I do not include the selection argument in inla.posterior.sample, then I can access samples from this specific predictor using 

samples=inla.posterior.sample(n=nsamp, result=m1)
inla.posterior.sample.eval(function(...) {Predictor[33]}, samples).

However, this uses much more memory.

Is there still a way to access the Predictor samples using inla.posterior.sample.eval when selection is applied in inla.posterior.sample?

Best wishes,
Daniel

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.posterior.sample.eval specific element of Predictor
parts:
Thanks Daniel,

you hit a weak point. In short, do not use ..eval when using
'selection'. Its a mess to define what is what in this case (as only a
subset of the samples are stored), and all this extra admin will just
kill any savings. I should have added a note about this in the help
page, and I will.

oops: using 'selection' only store a selection of the sample, but the
whole sample has to be generated in any case, so no computational
savings.


hope this helps, otherwise, let me know

Best
H

messages.author: a68f4a219f644d0b
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.posterior.sample.eval specific element of Predictor
parts:
Hi Håvard,

Thanks for your quick response!

No worries if this is not convenient to implement in inla.posterior.sample.eval.
Getting all variables in the output of inla.posterior.sample would only become a memory issue with very large datasets.

I have managed to get out the information from the samples object with selection in the following way.
samples=inla.posterior.sample(n=nsamp, result=m1, selection = list(Predictor=33))

For predictor 33:
predictor.samples=unlist(lapply(samples, function(x)(x$latent[1]))) 

For the hyperparameter:
hyper.samples=unlist(lapply(samples, function(x)(x$hyperpar[1])))

Best,
Daniel

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.posterior.sample.eval specific element of Predictor
parts:
I would like to get samples from posterior predictive, which can be obtained by adding the noise from the likelihood using the hyper parameter sample to the predictor, i.e. 
predictor.sample + Z*sigma.sample, where Z is a standard Gaussian, and sigma.sample is a sample from the standard deviation parameter (of the likelihood).

For this, I need samples from the joint distribution of the predictor and the standard deviation parameter, and I do not know how to get these without inla.posterior.sample.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] inla.posterior.sample.eval specific element of Predictor
parts:
Hi Daniel,

if the memory use for storing enough full samples is the limiting
factor, then I would suggest a block-wise approach; generate samples,
compute/simulate the functional you want, and either store just those
values, or if all you want are posterior mean&var or similar summary,
accumulate the information needed to compute those from multiple block
samples. This technique can also be used for quantiles, by using
recursive quantile estimators (I've been working towards an
implementation of that, for use cases like this).

Finn
